analysis.title: Weekly Investor Research: EM equity recovery dampened by US CPI and NVIDIA headwinds
key_insights: EM stocks rose 3.2% last week alongside a US tech relief rally. The recovery stalled after a hot US October CPI print and the resignation of NVIDIA CEO Jensen Huang on 12 November. MSCI EM ex-China rose 5.4% and MSCI China fell 4.6%.

Ashmore says EM tech valuations are very compelling and earnings growth estimates keep rising, so it is a good moment to add exposure while positioning is light. It expects tech and other risk assets to struggle to regain sustained momentum in the short term while financial conditions tighten.

The tightening backdrop is a US dollar up nearly 2% on the week, high UST yields and what looks like the start of a longer Fed hiking cycle. The curve bear-flattened, with the 10yr UST at 5.13% (+25bp) and the 2yr at 4.85% (+29bp).

US October CPI rose 0.4% mom against a 0.3% consensus, and core rose 0.3% for a third straight month. The BLS published no annual rates because of the 2025 shutdown, and estimates put headline at about 4.0% (from 3.7%) and core at about 2.8% (from 2.6%). Core was driven as much by demand-sensitive services as by energy or housing, which raises the risk that inflation is broadening.
Markets fully price a 25bp Fed hike for December and two more by September 2027. Waller said a 50bp December hike should be considered.

Huang resigned amid an affair admission and an independent board investigation into whether Alice Huang, a former Megaspeed managing director, passed information to Chinese intelligence. Ashmore says his departure is unlikely to set back NVIDIA's product pipeline, which looks set for two to three years. It calls NVIDIA's role as financial backer of neoclouds uncertain without him.

NVIDIA earnings on Tuesday are called another clearing event for markets. A broader US crackdown on NVIDIA's China business is possible, since Huang favoured a more open approach to China. NVIDIA is about 20% lower month to date and 32% below its all-time high at 11x 12-month forward earnings, the cheapest in over a decade. TSMC is down about 7.5% since the news broke.

A US-Iran breakthrough remains the key cross-asset trigger into year-end and looks further away than a week ago. Tehran called the US reply to its seven conditions insufficient and deceptive, and treats the US naval blockade as an act of war. Iran launched drones at Bahrain on 13 and 15 November. With oil in the USD 90s, markets price balanced risks, but the next move in the risk premium may tilt upward.

China October exports rose 35.2% yoy and imports 41.6%, helped by recovering Gulf crude shipments. Semiconductor exports rose 137% by value and autos 37.6%. The monthly surplus narrowed to USD 105.3bn from USD 133.5bn, and the January-October surplus is USD 1.04trn.

Taiwan October exports rose 58.9% yoy to a record USD 96.8bn, the 36th straight month of growth. ICT and audiovisual products rose 72.9% and integrated circuits 63.0%, together 83% of exports. Shipments to the US hit a record USD 32.9bn, 34% of the total.

The Megaspeed GPU smuggling scandal is set to bring tighter scrutiny of Asian data centres. The WSJ reported that US lawmakers may impose export rules and licensing on Malaysia, Thailand, Indonesia and Singapore. Malaysia has approved USD 95bn of data-centre projects since 2021 and is considering a chip-count reporting law.

The Bank of Korea held at 3.00% in October after hikes in July and August, with most members leaning hawkish. It expects 2026 and 2027 growth to significantly exceed its August forecasts of 3.3% and 2.9%, and another hike in November remains likely.

Peru's central bank surprised with a 25bp hike to 4.50%, its first move since August 2025. Lima inflation reached 5.25% yoy, and the bank said price pressures can no longer be seen as purely temporary but that the hike does not necessarily start a tightening cycle. Its next decision is on 10 December.

Brazil's Focus survey no longer expects Selic cuts this year and raised its end-2026 forecast to 13.75% from 13.50%. 2027 inflation expectations rose a fourth straight week to 4.90%, above the 4.50% ceiling. Copom is expected to hold at 13.75% on 8-9 December.

Colombia's board is split 4-3 and the 18 December decision looks a close call between a hold and a small hike. President de la Espriella said Colombia will drop plans to extend VAT coverage and the finance ministry is studying a headline VAT cut to 17-18% from 19%, despite the fiscal crisis.

Mexico's October inflation rose for a third month to 3.75% yoy against a 3.65% consensus, a week after Banxico's surprise 25bp cut to 6.25%. Trump threatened to double tariffs on Mexico over migrant caravans, which the peso largely ignored but which signals limited US urgency on the USMCA review.

Fitch named Ecuador among the Latin American economies most exposed to El Niño. The central bank estimates a moderate El Niño would cut 0.5pp from 2027 growth and a severe one about 1.4pp. Ecuador holds local elections on 29 November.

Poland MPC member Wnorowski said a December hike cannot be ruled out and a hike in early 2027 is highly probable, though a hold in December remains the base case. The CNB said the outlook justifies greater caution and expects inflation to jump temporarily well above 3% early next year.

S&P said Nigeria's goal of regaining investment grade by 2029 may be too ambitious, as no sovereign has moved from single-B to investment grade within three years. Egypt's urban inflation slowed to 12.7% yoy but monthly core accelerated to 1.2%, and the central bank has room to hold on 17 December.
Weekly cross-asset moves: Brent +3.7% to 96.0, gold -6.7% to 3,863, Bitcoin -13.1% to 64,591, DXY +1.8% to 103.4, EUR -1.9% and S&P 500 +2.5%. Brent is -18.4% month to date.
EM debt fell last week: GBI-EM GD -1.2% (driven by FX), EMBI GD -0.7% (driven by US rates), and EMBI GD spread 239 bps.

As NVIDIA's key supplier, TSMC is down about 7.5% since news of Huang's possible departure broke.

Ashmore describes positioning in tech stocks as light, which supports adding exposure.
Volatility in technology stocks continued, with a sharp Monday to Wednesday recovery interrupted by the CPI print and Huang's resignation.
geopolitical: US-Iran negotiations remain stalled. Tehran called the US reply to its seven conditions insufficient and deceptive, and Trump says he sees positive momentum and wants to maintain the status quo.

Iran treats the US naval blockade and US efforts to push tankers through the southern shipping lane as acts of war. It launched drones at Bahrain on 13 and 15 November in retaliation for US strikes on Iranian sites including Qeshm Island.
The Megaspeed GPU smuggling scandal and allegations of passing information to Chinese intelligence may lead the US to impose export rules and licensing on Malaysia, Thailand, Indonesia and Singapore.
Trump threatened to double tariffs on Mexico unless it stops migrant caravans, which suggests limited US urgency on the USMCA review.
Chinese exports to the US rose 32.9% and to the EU 24.3%, keeping trade imbalances in focus.

tension_points.bull_case: EM tech valuations are very compelling, earnings growth estimates continue to inflect higher and positioning remains light. NVIDIA trades at 11x forward earnings.
tension_points.bear_case: A rising dollar, high UST yields and a longer Fed hiking cycle make for a difficult backdrop, and hot CPI plus Huang's exit and a possible China crackdown stalled the recovery.
tension_points.what_invalidates: The report names no price level. The checkable events it flags are NVIDIA's Tuesday earnings, described as a clearing event, and a broader US crackdown on NVIDIA's China business.

tension_points.bear_case: Tehran rejected the US reply as insufficient and deceptive and treats the blockade as an act of war. Further attacks on shipping are possible, so the next move in the risk premium may tilt upward.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A US-Iran breakthrough, which the report calls the key trigger for cross-asset performance into year-end.
